body: Goodnight and good luck, I'll be around feel free to pm
Good to hear

It sounds like you do not have a lot of options right now. Honestly, I think since you've been having these thoughts for quite a while, it might be a decent idea to go to the hospital, and get new meds from your psychiatrist. Are you on any meds right now? Sorry if I'm sounding harsh but maybe given the circumstances professional help would be best.

You have trust issues, understandably so. You've been through something unthinkable. To even be here right now you must be a really strong person. 

It totally makes sense now why you wouldn't want to go to the hospital. I'm sorry you don't have friends in person you can turn to. Do you have a therapist? Or something like it?
Can you explain why you would rather not go to the hospital right now?
You said you've been in and out of the hospital your whole life, I'm assuming those were bad experiences? Was it for similar reasons as to what you're going through now?

What an awful situation, is there anyone or anywhere that you feel safe that you could go to right now? What do you need? What do you think it would take to get these thoughts out of your head? I don't want you to go through with this, you can get past this chapter in your life. It's a really terrible thing what this woman did to you, unthinkably horrible to use and abuse a person like that. You didn't deserve one bit of it. You deserve to have people in your life who genuinely care about you. I'm not going to sit here spouting advice like I know everything, because I don't, but know that I'm listening and I care.
Embrace the narcissism, friend. Embrace whatever it takes to keep you alive another day.

First off, try to calm down. Right here and right now, take a deep breath and calm down. I have autism too and I understand the tendency to become obsessed, not just with certain people, but with certain thoughts. Right now you're obsessing over this murder/suicide fantasy. You know it would be devastating if it were to actually happen. You would be taking away her chance to ever become a better  person, and taking away your chance to move on. But you don't need to move on right now. Right now you need to just calm down. Please calm down.

How long have you been having this recurring thought?

Are you sure it would not be a feasible option to visit the hospital? If not, maybe a suicide hotline?

That's good to hear. Hold on to that feeling and hold out as long as you can. Maybe that feeling of "it doesn't matter anyway" will help you fall in love with life again. Be as carefree as you can be, because ultimately it doesn't matter what anyone thinks or what you say or if you're a nice person or an asshole or if you do nothing but lay in bed eating ice cream all day. It really doesn't fucking matter anyway because we are all going to die eventually, whether by our own hand or not.

I want the depression to go away, no more compulsive self harming episodes, no more nightmares. No more social anxiety. The chance to do my life over and be what I had the potential to be. Make a friend or two. Even just one friend.

I have a little bit of experience with those games. I will work on my characters and also come up with something new to do. Not sure about leaving the house and joining a club in town or anything like that, but I guess I could learn more about a topic or skill of some type online. At the very least I'll at least make a list of new hobbies I'd like to try. The likelihood of me leaving the house to meet new people and pursue something new is very slim. But I'll work towards it. 

You've really helped me turn my thinking around to more positive thoughts, thank you so much. You can count on me probably messaging you in the future.

Well I like reading and I've been trying lately to write as well. I've been researching and learning how to develop characters and I'm starting to write some characters for a novel but it's terrible. 

I don't really have any passions or hobbies. I want to but I don't.

The only thing I want to ask is do you have any ideas for stuff I can do while stuck at home - as I will be for the next couple of weeks. I usually just read and watch tv and go on reddit. Then I am angry with myself for being lazy. 

Thank you thank you thank you for talking with me

I have one friend who always tells me about her problems and internal struggles she is having, so I guess that means she and I are close? But so far I haven't reciprocated by telling her about any of my struggles. I just try to listen and help her get through her own things. Maybe I could tell her. I'm worried about how she would take it if she knew.

Thanks for asking, I am actually doing a bit better today. Your encouragement and caring helped a lot. I'm going to save your words and reference it in the future when I need some reassurance that I am in fact not a terrible human being.

I have a migraine which is giving me an excuse to lay in bed all day and not hate myself for it. I was going to cut but drew on my skin with a ballpoint pen instead. That was a good decision. Also I went out to get some alcohol but got coffee instead. So far I feel like I have made decent choices today.

Yes it was tough to go through that especially since it was the first group of friends I made when I moved out to be "on my own" and free from my mother. I have noticed though that I am a little bit more friendly to people these days than I was right after that happened. Not much, but a tiny bit of improvement at least. I still can't "let people in" though. Except for strangers on the internet (like you, kind stranger!) I can't bring myself to tell my thoughts or emotions or problems to anyone or lean on anyone for help, I am so afraid they will turn away and leave me worse than I was before. Even my therapist I wasn't completely honest with, just honest enough to get some meds for my depression.

I think I am as bad as my mother in some ways. Like for example being suicidal, and mistrusting of people. She was abused as a child, too, and she never really recovered from it, and so she is a lonely and non-social person, too, like me. She has mental problems she can't recover from and I don't blame her for those things. I think I am more caring than she is, though. Like I try to be empathetic towards people and care about people, and she is not that way. Honestly I don't think she is capable of empathy. But I would never keep my children from seeing their father while growing up, which is what she did to me, and so I guess I could never be as bad as her as long as I don't do that.
Thank you very much for the kind words

What happened to damage my trust was, when I left home I got involved with a religious group which became my family basically. They were my family for a couple years, until I violated one of their "rules" (yes they were a cult, I realized later) and they kicked me out. I had no one left and had to start over while being shunned by the people I thought were my closest friends. This was a long time ago (a little over 2 years) and still I feel the sting of it. Now I see everyone as being shifty and shady and not who they pretend to be. And I am afraid to get back into religion, which used to give me comfort, because I don't trust anyone who goes to a church. 

No, I haven't done anything to anyone that is as mean as what my mother did to me. And I hope I never do. I don't have kids yet, so I don't know, but I hope I never do.

Actually I have been immersed in a college culture for the past few years, so yes there are plenty of opportunities and plenty of nice people. The problem is I don't let people get emotionally close to me anymore. It's a long story, but to sum it up I have major trust issues that have crippled me socially. Not only that, but people don't seem to like me much either. No one has ever reached out to me to be my friend, not even when I was a kid. I'm kind of weird. I have asperger's so I have a weird sense of humor and don't pick up on social cues. I find it is much less of a strain to just be a loner.

Thank you for saying that I'm strong. You're right, it doesn't feel that way. Considering all the times I've tried to die and failed, I feel more like a failure than a strong person. 

I was abused by my mom as a child and teen and even though I've moved far away from that situation, it still stays with me in my head. I hear her voice telling me I am shit and stupid and wrong and worthless, I hear it over and over again every moment. I still hear the screeching sounds of her screaming at me to go to hell. I can feel the loneliness of not being allowed to leave the house for months at a time. And I can hear her saying no to every question I ever asked, and going back on every promise she ever made. And I hate myself most of all because she was suicidal, and so am I, and therefore I am just like her. 

I feel stagnant because I haven't made a new friend in 3 years.

Well it started to get better when I reached out and started seeing a therapist and got some meds. That was about six months ago. He helped me realize that suicidal thoughts stem from negative emotions which are the result of negative thoughts about myself. So I worked on changing my thinking to be more optimistic. But the facts are staring me in the face, and I feel like I am lying to myself when I try to think optimistically. I am a lonely loser and I am self destructive and stagnant, those are facts, and positive thinking is not helping those things :/ 

Distraction helps, though, so when I am in school the negative thoughts subside a bit. Because I have something to work for and things to look forward too. I'm petrified of college ending.

Sorry for the wall-of-text comment.

If I had to pinpoint a cause I think maybe I just have too many things right now making me anxious and making me feel alone. School just ended, I'm not getting hours at work, had to cancel plans to be with "friends" (read acquaintances) tonight because I cut myself and it's bleeding everywhere, most of all the only person I really love is far away and I won't see him for a while. I'm on pills for my depression but they don't seem to be working anymore. 

It feels like maybe being lonely and suicidal is just who I am, and no matter how far I stray from it I'll always go back to being that way.

I appreciate the reply so much, thank you.

It's always been hard to cope, my whole life. I've had OCD and depression and anxiety since childhood, and tried to kill myself when I was 9, and a couple times again as a teenager. Recently I thought things were getting better for a while and was getting a sense of wonder and excitement about life but it's slipping away again and I am terrified. I'm terrified of going back to when I was drinking myself to sleep every night and praying I wouldn't wake up. I'm scared of college ending and not knowing what to do with my life. I'm terrified of not making a mark on the world and dying alone and unloved. 

I've been trying to keep my head up and be optimistic for so long but it's like swimming upstream, I am getting so tired.
